_comment: Read by scripts/public-data-audit.mjs. On the Sanity free plan a dataset is
PUBLIC: anyone can read every published document over a plain URL, with no
token, and the project id ships in the page source. This file records what we
have deliberately decided is fine to publish, and why.
Every entry needs a reason. The point is that the judgement gets made once,
in daylight, rather than by whoever is looking at a red build at 9pm.
blockedTypes: never public, whatever fields they carry. Use for anything
holding member or family data - the audit fails if even one is readable.
allowedTypes: a type that trips the personal-data heuristics but is genuinely
publishable, listing the exact fields that are allowed.
_forkNote: The template's "noDataset": true line is deleted here, as the template says a
fork must. This site has a real project (7iynvqq6) and a real public dataset,
so the audit has something to audit and an audit that skips would report a

race.reason: The venue address of a public city park (Mt. Airy Forest, 5083 Colerain Ave). It is the start line, it is printed on the site on purpose, and it belongs to Cincinnati Parks rather than to a person.

page.reason: Page copy names roads and the venue when telling entrants how to get there. No person's address appears in it.

athlete.reason: Race results. 721 finishers, each carrying the name, city and state their timer recorded, imported from RunSignUp's own PUBLIC results pages where the identical data already sits. Publishing finishing times under a runner's name is what a results archive is, and entrants supply it knowing that. Recorded here deliberately rather than left to the heuristics: the audit does not currently flag a bare `name` field, so without this entry the decision would never have been made in daylight. NOTE for whoever reads this next: no date of birth, no email, no address, and no ages beyond the age-on-race-day the results already publish. If a runner ever asks to be removed, delete their athlete document and re-run the import with their result_id excluded, because a plain re-import would restore them.

siteSettings.reason: The organisation's own postal address and phone, printed in the site footer.
